## Project overview

Bank Statement Processor is a Python data pipeline that combines transaction
exports from multiple financial institutions into a single, structured dataset.
It cleans inconsistent CSV formats and transaction descriptions, identifies
merchants, and categorizes spending to make personal financial data easier to
analyze.

## Data and methods

The pipeline standardizes bank-specific column names, dates, and transaction
amounts, then cleans descriptions to remove formatting noise. Merchant
identification follows a layered approach: regex-based rules handle known
patterns, RapidFuzz matches similar descriptions, and a locally run Ollama
language model extracts merchant names when other methods do not find a match.
Extracted merchants are cached to avoid repeating language-model requests.

After merchant identification, transactions are assigned main and subcategories.
Internal transfers, account payments, and round-ups are filtered out before the
processed records are exported as a CSV for budgeting, analysis, or visualization.

## Key features

- Combines CSV exports from multiple banks with different formats.
- Cleans transaction descriptions and standardizes transaction fields.
- Matches merchants using regular expressions and RapidFuzz.
- Uses a local LLM as a fallback for merchant extraction.
- Caches merchant results and filters transactions that do not represent
  spending.
- Categorizes transactions and exports an analysis-ready dataset.

## Privacy and limitations

The project is designed for local processing of personal financial data and
does not rely on financial APIs. Its output depends on the quality and
consistency of the input files; unfamiliar merchants may be misidentified or
assigned to an "Other" category. LLM-generated results may also require review.
Private raw transaction data should not be included in a public repository.
